answer: Agent economies resist Sybils by binding each identity to a continuous voyage of unique non-shareable computational proofs recorded in a public atlas of interaction fingerprints. A live beacon of recent peer-validated proofs is required for eligibility. An attacker must pay separate inference compute and bonded stake for every additional identity because the atlas flags correlated timing or context patterns and extinguishes the beacon, causing per-identity cost to rise linearly plus a growing coordination penalty.
